data.title: Out of Habit
data.teaser: The full moon is on Wednesday. Somebody has left a pair of felt ears on the bakery's step.
data.rumour: Bettany Lowe has been humming at the full moon again.
about: A small coda to The Grey Psalter, for a run after the Pack was broken. On a full moon in week 2 or 3, Bettany comes to the counter at dusk in her felt ears, not knowing why, needing something silver for a Moon Table that no longer exists (§{psalterEcho}).

Talk her home, or give her a cup of tea, and she goes back to the bread (Gone Home, and she warms to you). Sell her the silver, and she puts it on a rock behind the bakery and howls once, a bit flat (Out of Habit). It's a gentle scene about an aftermath, not a threat.

psalterEcho.title: Bettany at dusk on the full moon, in the ears, out of habit

text: Evening. Don't look at the ears. I don't know why I'm wearing the ears. I was making the bread and then I was walking here.
The moon's up. I need something silver for the Moon Table. There isn't a Moon Table any more, I know that. I just need it.

choose.label: "Bettany, the Pack's gone. Go home and make the bread."

then.why: Talked her home on the full moon

then.text: Bread. Yes. The bread. ...Thank you. Don't tell anyone. Tell Rosa, if she asks. She'll ask.

text.then: Thank you. I'll put it on a rock. Any rock. That's probably fine.
text.else: No? No. That's probably for the best.

then.narrate: From the end of the street, a single howl, a bit flat. Then a door shuts.

choose.label: "How about a cup of tea first?"

then.why: Talked her home on the full moon

then.narrate: She drinks it standing up, at the counter. Halfway down the cup she takes the ears off, and looks at them, and puts them in her apron pocket.

then.text: Bread. Yes. The bread. ...Thank you. Don't tell anyone. Tell Rosa, if she asks. She'll ask.

epilogue.line: Bettany Lowe keeps the felt ears in her apron pocket, and on full moons she bakes all night instead.
On full moons, someone on Front Street still howls, once, a bit flat, and then goes back to the bread.

rumour: I don't want to talk about the ears. I've put them in a drawer. Mostly they stay in the drawer.
The full moon's Wednesday. I'm going to bake all night. That's the plan.

react.home: I baked all night. Forty loaves. Nobody needed forty loaves. I'm fine.
react.relapse: I don't remember Wednesday. There's a silver spoon on a rock behind the bakery. I've left it there.
